• Dose: 150 mg every 4–6 h (max 4 doses/day).
  – Tylenol Children's / Infants', syrup 160 mg/5 ml: 4.6 ml
  – syrup 120 mg/5 ml: 6.2 ml
  – syrup 125 mg/5 ml: 6 ml
  – syrup 150 mg/5 ml (3 %): 5 ml

q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to children over 6 months old, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. The SEUP adds that the dose is the one your paediatrician recommends, and that the goal is your child's comfort rather than bringing the fever down on its own [2].

Do not give ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor has said it is OK [3]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [3].

Get medical advice if:
- Your child is not their usual self or is not interested in feeding [3]
- They show signs of dehydration, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, or no tears when crying [3]
- The fever lasts 5 days or more [3]
- You are worried, or the medicine is not helping [4]

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Vomiting twice in a morning is often gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious in healthy people but can sometimes lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2].

What to do now: the priority is to keep fluids going in. Wait 20 minutes after a vomit, then give oral rehydration solution, 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, says the SEUP [3]. If he keeps it down, you can slowly increase how often you offer it [3]. Don't use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3]. Keep offering his normal food in smaller, more frequent amounts; no need to fast, and dairy and breastfeeding are fine [4]. Sports drinks should be avoided [4].

Get help if:
- He vomits a lot, can't keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without drinking [7]
- Vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [7]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or urinates little [7]
- Severe belly pain or headache [7]
- Under 3 months old and has vomited two or more feeds [7]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
The biggest risk from vomiting is dehydration, which happens when a child loses more fluid than they take in [1][3].

What to do now: give an oral rehydration solution. After your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [4]. If they keep it down, you can slowly offer it more often [4]. Don't use homemade drinks like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [4]. Keep breastfeeding normally, and offer small, frequent meals — no need to fast [5].

Signs to watch for and get help:
- Drowsy, limp or very thirsty [7]
- Sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [7]
- Vomiting a lot, can't keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without drinking [7]
- Green vomit, blood, or brown coffee-ground material [7]
- Under 3 months old and vomited two or more feeds [7]

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common with colds and flu, and both usually get better on their own [3][5]. For a 5-year-old, the things that help are simple: offer plenty of fluids, let them rest, and run a clean humidifier or cool-mist vaporizer in the room [3]. Saline nose drops or spray can also ease a blocked nose [3].

Be careful with cough and cold medicines: some contain ingredients not recommended for children, so talk to your child's doctor before giving any [3]. Never give aspirin to a child [3].

Get medical help if your child has:
- Trouble breathing or fast breathing [3]
- Signs of dehydration [3]
- Fever lasting more than 4 days [3]
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days with no improvement [3]
- Symptoms that improve, then come back or get worse [3]

Coughing that is worse at night can also be a sign of asthma in children [4].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough lasting about a week after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days [6]. In whooping cough, the first signs are also cold-like — runny nose, mild fever, mild occasional cough — and last 1 to 2 weeks before the cough gets worse [3].

What to do now: keep offering fluids, and keep the room free of smoke and fumes, which can trigger coughing [1]. There is no home treatment in these sources that shortens a cough; if you are worried, your doctor can assess your son.

Get medical care if:
- Coughing fits that are worse at night, or a high-pitched "whoop" between coughs [3][4]
- Vomiting during or after coughing fits [3]
- Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout, or turning blue or grey [4]
- A pause in breathing (apnea) in a baby [3]
- Cough getting worse instead of better after a week [3][4]

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without fever, with normal eating, is usually a mild illness — fever is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1]. Keep offering fluids and normal meals; a poor diet for a few days won't hurt [3].

Watch for these signs and get help if they appear:
- Fever of 38°C (100.4 °F) or higher in a baby under 3 months [1]
- Fever lasting 5 days or more [1]
- Not wanting to eat, or not their usual self [1]
- Dehydration — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears [1]
- Difficulty breathing, or skin/lips turning blue or grey [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly should be checked by a doctor, since the information available does not describe what causes them or how they usually progress.

While you arrange that, keep your daughter comfortable and let her keep her normal activity if she is otherwise well [4]. Offer fluids and watch her nappies or toilet visits so you know when she last passed urine and how her stools look [4].

Get medical help if she has any of these:
- Looks unwell, floppy, pale, or refuses food [6]
- Stomach pain that is continuous or getting worse, or that wakes her at night [2]
- Pain on the right side of the abdomen [2]
- Repeated vomiting that is green, brown or bloody [2]
- Black, tar-like stools or blood in the stool [2]
- A tense, hard or swollen abdomen [2]

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Itchy red bumps on the legs are common in small children, and one cause is eczema, which most often causes dry, itchy skin and rashes, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Scratching can make the skin red, swollen and itch even more [2]. Eczema is not contagious [2].

What helps: keep the skin well cared for and avoid things that irritate it, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, stress, and things your child is allergic to like foods, pollen and animals [2]. Treatments may include medicines, skin creams and light therapy [2].

See your doctor if:
- The rash spreads or gets worse [2]
- The skin becomes very red, swollen or itchy despite care [2]
- Your child seems unwell or the itching disturbs sleep [2]
sources: [2] MedlinePlus — "Eczema" (2025), p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/eczema.html

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that spread or increase over days can have several causes, and the pattern matters more than the spots themselves. Scabies causes intensely itchy bumps and lines, worse at night, on fingers, wrists, arms, legs and around the waist, according to the WHO [1]. Eczema causes dry, itchy skin with a rash on the face, inside the elbows, behind the knees, hands and feet, and it is not contagious, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Measles rash starts as flat red spots at the hairline and spreads downward, usually with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, according to the CDC [5].

See your doctor if:
- The spots keep spreading or multiplying each day [1][5]
- She develops fever, cough, runny nose or red eyes [5][6]
- The skin becomes raw, scaly, or she seems uncomfortable or distressed [3][4]
- The spots become crusty, weepy or look infected [1]

A doctor can look at the rash and tell you what it is and how to treat it.

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [2][6]. For the next 24 hours, watch him closely for any sign that something is wrong [3].

What you can do now: he can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Keep him resting from sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return to normal activities gradually [4].

Get medical help now if he:
- has been knocked out or cannot stay awake [2]
- has a seizure, or new weakness or numbness [2]
- is vomiting repeatedly [4]
- is confused, or hard to wake [4]
- has clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears [4]
- has trouble walking, speaking or balancing [2]

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Around 6 months, breast milk or formula alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods should start now, according to the WHO [1]. At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating; they still get most energy and nutrients from milk [2].

Start with small amounts and increase gradually as your baby grows, and build up the consistency and variety of foods over time [1]. Offer 2–3 meals a day at this age [1]. Introduce one food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting [5].

Keep giving breast milk or formula alongside the solids [2].

Avoid these:
- Honey before age 1 (risk of botulism) [5]
- Cow's milk before age 1 [5]
- Unpasteurised drinks or foods [5]
- Choking hazards: sweets, popcorn, whole nuts, whole grapes [5]

Ask your baby's doctor when to start and about peanut-containing foods if there is eczema or egg allergy [5].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and water is not needed in large amounts. The AEP says that between 6 and 12 months breast milk remains the main food and should be kept on demand, without reducing the number of feeds [2]. If a baby over 6 months has at least 4–5 breastfeeds a day, no other milk source is needed [2].

What to do now: keep offering breast milk or formula on demand, and give water only in small amounts with meals, from a cup. During an illness, the WHO says to increase fluid intake, including how often you breastfeed, and to offer soft, favourite foods [1].

When to get help:
- Fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, or a dry mouth [1]
- Refusing all feeds or drinks [1]
- Vomiting or diarrhoea that will not stop [1]
- Sleepy, floppy, or hard to wake [1]
- Fever in a baby this age [1]

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the way to build liking for vegetables is repeated, varied exposure rather than pressure. The AEP advises introducing the whole variety of fruits and vegetables gradually, at any daily meal, and varying how they are offered — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [1]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is formed early, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [1]. Offer vegetables alongside fruit at meals, and keep offering them even if refused; the NHS suggests including vegetables with bitter flavours such as broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage [3]. Give whole fruit rather than juice, since juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods [1]. For green leafy vegetables like spinach or chard in the first year, keep them under 20% of the dish because of nitrates [1].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula alone no longer meets a child's energy and nutrient needs: around 6 months those needs start to exceed what milk provides, and complementary foods are needed to cover them [2]. The WHO guiding principles are to keep breastfeeding (or formula) on demand up to 2 years or more, while giving solid foods from 6 months [2][3].

What to do now: offer 3–4 meals a day plus 1–2 snacks as needed, starting with small amounts and gradually increasing quantity, consistency and variety [2]. Feed to appetite, following hunger and fullness cues, and keep good hygiene when handling food [2].

See your doctor if you are worried about her growth or eating — the AEP notes that if complementary foods are not introduced around 6 months, or are given too early, growth can be affected [2].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differs from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. It is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day [3].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Your baby's doctor will want to keep an eye on constipation unless it comes with any of these signs [3]:

- Important belly pain, or a baby who is very down and complaining a lot [3]
- Blood in the stool [3]
- Vomiting many times, not keeping down solids or liquids [3]
- Pain when passing stool [3]

Call your doctor if you notice any of these.

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
Waking every two hours at night is common at this age: night wakings are physiological, and around 30% of children still wake at night by one year, according to PUC Chile [1]. The usual cause in healthy babies is habit — how they fall asleep — rather than illness [6].

What helps: put your baby down still awake, so they learn to fall asleep on their own; if they always fall asleep in your arms, they will look for that same condition when they wake [1]. If they wake, give them the chance to settle back by themselves before going in [1]. Sleep cycles last about 90 minutes [1].

See your doctor if:
- Waking comes with fever, poor feeding or unusual irritability [6]
- Symptoms of reflux, cow's milk allergy or ear infection [6]
- You feel the waking is affecting your baby's or the family's wellbeing [6]

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on at night or early in the morning is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [5]. In preschoolers, the most common trigger of this kind of cough and wheeze is a viral respiratory infection, according to the SEUP [1].

What to do now: keep giving fluids and keep the room free of tobacco smoke, since children of smokers get more respiratory illnesses [7]. If your child has been prescribed a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, it must be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [7]. The dose is the one your doctor or the leaflet gives.

See a doctor if:
- Your child is very restless or drowsy, or turns blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, the ribs show, or the chest sucks in [7]
- Inhalations are needed every two hours or less [7]
- Severe coughing or serious trouble breathing [5]

If there is no clear improvement after treatment, go to a health centre [7].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using albuterol more often than usual can be a sign the asthma is not fully controlled, and the SEUP says inhalers should always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth, because they work less well that way [7]. Keep giving the albuterol with a spacer and mask for small children, and avoid smoke and allergens during the flare [3]. The WHO notes that most people with asthma need their inhaler daily, and that steroid inhalers reduce the risk of severe attacks [2].

Get medical help if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs show, belly moves a lot, or chest sinks in [7]
- Inhalers needed every two hours or less [7]
- No clear improvement after albuterol [7]

The dose depends on your child's weight; follow the dose your doctor or the leaflet gives.

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, an inflammation of the voice box and windpipe that often starts like a cold and causes noisy, sharp sounds when breathing in, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It is usually caused by a virus and most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3]. Symptoms often get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Keep your child calm and comfortable, and offer fluids often. Croup often starts as a cold, so watch how she breathes over the next few days [3].

Get help if:
- Breathing becomes difficult or she is breathing fast [1][4]
- The ribs pull in or the chest sinks with each breath [1][2][4]
- She seems drowsy, very irritable or generally unwell [1][4]
- She refuses to eat or drink [4]
- You are worried about her breathing [3]

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can have several causes, and one of them is asthma: chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply is a common symptom, according to the WHO [2]. Symptoms like these should be discussed with a healthcare provider [2].

If your child has a cold or a cough along with it, watch for these signs at home: breathing that is fast, ribs pulling in, or the chest sinking in, and chest pain when breathing [1]. Also watch for tiredness when walking or running [1].

Get medical help if:
- He seems generally unwell, drowsy, or very irritable [1][5]
- Breathing becomes difficult, with fast breathing, ribs showing, or the chest sinking in [1][5]
- Chest or side pain when breathing [5]
- He refuses food and fluids [5]
- His colour looks wrong [5]

q: my baby has a temperature of 100.4, is that considered a fever

100.4 °F = 38 °C.

If your baby is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older baby, a temperature of 100.4 °F (38 °C (100.4 °F)) is considered a fever, according to the NHS [3].

Fever is not a disease — it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers in children are caused by common illnesses like coughs and colds [5][6]. You can usually look after them at home, and the temperature should come down over 1 to 4 days [2].

- They are 3 to 6 months and have a temperature of 39 °C (102.2 °F) or higher [5].
- They have a rash along with the fever [5].

- They are not feeding, not themselves, or show signs of dehydration [5].

text:

- Persistent vomiting or vomiting even without taking anything [1]

q: my son missed his 4 month vaccines, what do we do now
text:
A missed vaccine dose does not mean starting over: the child should receive the same schedule as other babies, with the same timing, according to the AEP [2]. The unit dose of each vaccine is the same as for any other baby, and there is no basis for reduced or split doses [1].

What to do now: book an appointment with your doctor or clinic to catch up. Between doses of the same vaccine there should be an interval of 4 weeks to 6 months depending on the vaccine, though the minimum is usually around 8 weeks [6]. The ages in the schedule follow the United States national schedule.

Get help or advice if:
- Your child is unwell with a fever or infection — vaccination may need to be temporarily postponed [1].

103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children get better within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [5]. The goal at home is your child's comfort, not bringing the number down by itself [3].

Keep offering plenty of fluids in small amounts, dress them lightly and don't overbundle them, and don't force food if they don't want it [3]. - Fever lasts more than 4 days [5]
- A seizure or fit happens [5]
- They seem very unwell, floppy or hard to wake [5]

If one is not helping your child's symptoms, you can try the other instead, as long as it is suitable for your child [2]. q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible — a thermometer reading that high means the measurement is wrong, so check it again. Fever itself is not an illness: it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections [1]. Fever is very common in young children [3].

If your child does have a fever, take the temperature with a digital thermometer, in the armpit or rectally, which is most accurate [5]. Before treating it, look at how your child is: if there are no warning signs, start with physical measures — remove extra clothing, give fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath if your child is comfortable [5]. Fever rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) on its own [5].

Get medical help if your child is very sleepy, confused, irritable or behaving abnormally, or has a severe headache or repeated vomiting [6].

- Your child has a weakened immune system [2]

- Symptoms that get worse instead of better [3]

- Difficulty breathing or a high-pitched sound when breathing [7]

It is normal for a 9-month-old not to have teeth yet. A first tooth usually appears between 4 and 8 months, but that is only the usual range, according to MedlinePlus [4].

Until then, wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal, and don't put them to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. As soon as the first tooth shows, switch to a soft toothbrush [4]. Once teeth are through, brush them at least twice a day, especially before bed, and do the real brushing yourself [1]. q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Chickenpox is very contagious, and children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of it, according to the CDC [1]. A child can pass it on until all the spots have crusted over, so they should stay home until then [2].

While he is home: calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help with the itching, and acetaminophen can help with fever. Do not give aspirin — with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [3].

See a doctor if:
- The rash looks infected or very painful [3]
- He has trouble breathing or seems very unwell [3]
- He is a baby, a teenager, or has a weakened immune system — these cases can be more serious [3]

Most children recover fully, and once they have had chickenpox they are usually immune for life [1].

q: she bumped her forehead on the table and cried right away, do I need to watch her
text:
A bump on the forehead is usually minor, because the skull is hard and protects the brain, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous, and no tests are usually needed, according to the SEUP [4].

What to do now: watch her over the first 24 hours for any sign of something more serious [4]. She can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking her every 4 hours [5]. If she has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [5]. She can eat and drink as usual, according to her appetite [5]. Most children recover quickly [5].

Get help if:

Make sure she drinks plenty of fluids, keep her room at a neutral temperature and ventilated, and avoid over-bundling her [2]. - has a fever lasting 5 days or more [7]
- has a rash along with the fever [7]

Keep breastfeeding — offer the breast normally, and even more often if your baby wants it, according to the SEUP [1]. There is no need to stop feeding or to fast your baby; feed smaller amounts more frequently and let their appetite guide you [1]. The NHS says to carry on breastfeeding and to give small amounts more often than usual [5]. If your baby is taking fluids well, you can offer food in small amounts, without forcing, and avoid fizzy drinks and sugary juices [3].

Get help if:
- Your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [4]
- They vomit a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomit even without taking anything [4]
- The vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [4]
- They are drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, have sunken eyes, cry without tears, or pee little [4]
- There is severe tummy pain or headache [4]

q: what temperature counts as a fever in a newborn
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Baby under 3 months with fever (≥38 °C / 100.4 °F)
text:
A fever in a baby this young is a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher, according to the NHS [3]. Babies under 3 months with a temperature that high need to be seen by a doctor the same day [2].

While you wait to be seen, keep breastfeeding as normal and offer plenty of fluids [4]. Do not undress your baby or sponge them down to cool them, and do not wrap them in too many clothes or blankets [2]. Do not give paracetamol to a baby under 2 months, and do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months [2].

Get help urgently if your baby:
- has a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it [2]
- has a stiff neck, is bothered by light, or has a fit [2]
- has unusually cold hands and feet, or blue, grey or blotchy skin or lips [2]
- is drowsy and hard to wake, or is not feeding or responding normally [2]
- has difficulty breathing, including grunting or stomach sucking under the ribs [2]

q: my son passed out after standing in the sun for a long time
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Not responding to stimuli
text:
Fainting can happen when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, and heat, standing still for a long time, or standing up suddenly can bring it on, according to the SEUP [2]. The child may go pale, stop responding and lose strength, and may have 2 or 3 jerks of the arms and legs [3].

While you get help: move him to a cool place, remove clothing, use damp cloths or a fan to help him lose heat, and give fluids to drink [6]. If he is not fully alert, do not give anything by mouth.

Get help now if you see:
- Skin hot, red and dry, or fever above 39°C (102.2 °F) [5]
- Confusion or disorientation [5]
- Severe headache [5]
- Nausea or vomiting [5]
- Loss of consciousness [5]

q: my toddler is struggling to breathe and the ribs are pulling in

text:
A toddler who is breathing hard enough for the ribs to pull in needs to be checked now, according to the SEUP [2][3].

While you get help: keep your child upright and calm, and do not give anything by mouth if they are struggling to breathe [3].

Signs the SEUP says mean it is serious:
- Ribs pulling in, chest sinking, or the belly moving with each breath [2][3]
- Breathing fast, or tiring when walking or running [2]
- Floppy, sleepy, or very irritable [2][3]
- Chest or side pain when breathing [3]
- A bad colour [3]

q: my 2 year old fell off the sofa and was sick once
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
A head injury is a blow to the head, usually from a fall, and vomiting is one of the symptoms it can cause, according to the SEUP [1]. While you get your child seen, keep them calm and watch them closely; the SEUP advises staying at rest, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours after the blow, with no sports and no screens [5].

Signs that mean it is getting worse, from the SEUP [5]:
- Severe or worsening headache that does not ease with paracetamol or ibuprofen
- Repeated vomiting
- Confusion or disorientation; in small children, irritability or being hard to wake
- Changes in usual behaviour, trouble speaking or walking
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears

MedlinePlus also lists repeated vomiting or nausea, worsening headache, seizures, dilated pupils, weakness in arms or legs, and growing confusion as reasons to get help immediately [4].

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Red, itchy patches on the arms are often eczema, which MedlinePlus describes as dry, itchy skin that scratching can make redder and more swollen [1]. It is not contagious [1].

What helps: keep the skin moisturised and avoid things that irritate it, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, and stress [1]. Treatments can include medicines, skin creams and light therapy, alongside good skin care [1].

See your doctor if:
- The patches do not get better in about a month [2]
- The skin becomes crusted, oozes pus, or sores spread — this can be a bacterial infection such as impetigo, which needs antibiotics [6]
- The itching is severe or the skin is cracked and sore [2]

q: my toddler is wheezing after running around outside
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: symptoms often start after physical effort, and in preschool children the main cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections, according to the SEUP [2][7]. Asthma can also cause wheezing, cough and chest tightness [3].

What to do now: keep your child calm and sitting upright, and let them rest — do not make them run or play until they are better. Offer small sips of water. If your child has been prescribed a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, give it as your doctor or the leaflet instructs; the dose depends on your child's weight [2].

Get help now if you notice:
- Chest pulling in, ribs or collarbones showing with each breath [7]
- Breathing faster than normal [7]
- Blue colour around the lips [7]
- Great difficulty breathing, continuous cough, or trouble speaking [7]
- Intense cough, severe breathing problems, or pale or bluish face, lips and nails [4]

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
Earache after a cold is often an ear infection: the middle ear, behind the eardrum, gets infected and inflamed, usually as a complication of a cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5].

Keep your child comfortable and give plenty to drink. If they have a fever, they can go back to school once they have been 24 hours without fever [4].

See a doctor if:
- They seem very down, sleepy or very irritable [4]
- They have trouble breathing [4]
- The earache is severe, or there is fluid or discharge from the ear
- The pain does not improve, or they keep getting fevers

The dose of any medicine depends on your child's weight, so follow what your doctor or the leaflet gives.

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
banner: 🚨 Call 999 / 112 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Unable to drink or breastfeed: it is one of the IMNCI danger signs — get seen today
text:
A blocked nose is common with a cold, and it can make feeding harder for a baby [3]. Saline nose drops from a pharmacy can help when the nose is blocked, according to the NHS [4]. Keep the nose clear with nasal washes, and feed in small, frequent amounts to keep feeding and hydration up [2]. Hold your baby in a semi-upright position to make breathing easier [2]. If there is fever and your baby is uncomfortable, children's paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given — check the leaflet to make sure it suits your child [4]. Avoid all exposure to tobacco smoke, and wash hands often to stop the virus spreading [2].

Get help if your baby:
- cannot drink or breastfeed [1]
- is feeding poorly and needs a feeding check within 5 days [1]
- has severe palmar pallor [1]

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39.2°C with cold hands is a reason to get your child seen today, according to the NHS [6]. While you arrange that, keep offering plenty of fluids and do not force them to eat [2].

Watch for these signs and get help straight away if any appear:
- Breathing fast, grunting, or the tummy sucking under the ribs [6]
- Pauses in breathing [6]
- Skin, tongue or lips blue or grey [6]
- Floppy and will not wake up or stay awake [6]
- Dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or other signs of dehydration [6]

A child who is very tired, irritable or not themselves also needs urgent advice [6]. Trust your own judgement if your child seems seriously unwell [6].

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text:
Yes, you can give ibuprofen (Nurofen) instead if paracetamol is not helping, according to the NHS [6]. Do not give both at the same time, but you can alternate between them if a doctor or nurse tells you to [6]. Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose — check the packet or leaflet [6].

Ibuprofen is usually given every 6 to 8 hours, and the dose goes by weight, not age [4]. It should not be given if your child is vomiting repeatedly, or if they are under 3 months or under 5 kg [4].

Get medical advice if:
- You have given more paracetamol than the packet, leaflet or prescription says [7]
- Your child is under 5 years old and you need urgent advice [7]

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache with no appetite is common in children, and the SEUP says it is usually temporary [7]. It often comes with fever, vomiting, diarrhoea or cough, and sometimes it is caused by an illness outside the belly, like a sore throat or an ear infection [1].

What helps now: offer small sips of oral rehydration solution often, and give the amount you were told after each loose stool or vomit — small, frequent amounts are tolerated best [4]. Don't force food.

See a doctor if your child:
- is generally unwell, sluggish or pale [7]
- refuses food markedly [7]
- has severe belly pain [5]
- has signs of dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, peeing less, no tears when crying [5]
- has diarrhoea lasting more than a day, or frequent vomiting [5]

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more is one of the signs of dehydration in babies, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Dehydration happens when a child loses more fluid than they take in, and diarrhoea, vomiting and fever are common causes [3].

Keep offering fluids: breastfeed normally, and more often if your baby wants it [1]. If your baby struggles to keep fluids down, try small sips of water or pieces of ice to suck [2]. Oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription and replace the fluids and salts lost [4]. Do not give sports drinks — they have too much sugar and the wrong salts for a baby with diarrhoea [1].

Warning signs in babies and young children:
- Dry mouth and tongue [6]
- Crying without tears [6]
- No wet nappies for 3 hours or more [6]
- Unusual sleepiness or irritability [6]
- Sunken eyes [6]

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home [2]. For a baby under 6 months, a fever of 38°C or higher needs medical advice — the NHS says to get urgent advice for a baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher, and for a baby of 3 to 6 months with a temperature of 39°C or higher [7].

While you wait to be seen: keep breastfeeding as normal or give plenty of fluids, check on your baby regularly including during the night, and keep them at home [2]. Do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [7]. Paracetamol can be given to babies over 2 months if they are distressed or uncomfortable — check the leaflet or ask a pharmacist or doctor, and never give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months [2][7].

Get help now if your baby:
- has a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it [7]
- has a stiff neck, is bothered by light, or has a fit [7]
- is drowsy and hard to wake, or is extremely agitated [7]
- has cold hands and feet, or blue, grey or blotchy skin or lips [7]
- is not feeding or not interested in normal activities [7]

text:
A fall from a bed and vomiting twice means your son needs to be checked today, and the SEUP says a fall from more than a metre or a child under three months should always be seen in the emergency department [1]. - He vomits green fluid, blood, or something like coffee grounds [2]

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most mosquito bites are harmless and usually just itch, according to MedlinePlus [2]. To calm the itch, a zinc and calamine lotion with menthol, phenol or camphor can be applied, or a short course of a topical corticosteroid such as hydrocortisone [5]. An oral antihistamine can also help with the itching and swelling [5]. To keep mosquitoes away, use a repellent containing DEET, icaridine or IR3535, cover the skin with clothing, and use screens or nets, according to the WHO [6].

See a doctor if:
- The bite looks infected [4]
- There is a serious allergic reaction [4]
- Your daughter seems unwell or feverish [4]

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and asthma is one of them: coughing that is worse at night or early in the morning is a symptom of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [4]. The NHS also lists coughing that is worse at night as a sign of asthma [6].

There is nothing in these sources about using a nebulizer for a night cough, so whether one is needed is a decision for your doctor.

What may help at home: water can ease a cough, whether your child drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Children under four should not have cough medicine [5].

See your doctor if:
- Your child has asthma symptoms [6]
- Symptoms are waking them at night [6]
- A very bad cough that is getting worse [7]
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [7]
- Hard or shallow breathing, or chest pain when breathing [7]

दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण है, और यह इलाज योग्य है [4][7]। WHO के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) से करें — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है [2]। साथ ही ज़िंक की गोलियाँ दी जाती हैं, जो दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% कम करती हैं [2][4]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें: पोषक भोजन — स्तनपान सहित — दस्त के दौरान भी जारी रखें [2]। SEUP के अनुसार खाना थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार दें, ताकि उल्टी का खतरा कम हो, और बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करें [6]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें; डेयरी उत्पाद ज़रूरी नहीं कि बंद करें, और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, माँगने पर और भी बार-बार कराएँ [6]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [6]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बहुत उल्टी हो, तरल भी न पचे [6]
- उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो [6]
- दस्त 14 दिन या ज़्यादा चलें [4]
- मल में खून हो [2]
- निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखें [2]
sources: [2] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[4] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Overview", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/f
[6] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE
[7] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Key facts", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने में मन न लगना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह में छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे लाल दाने निकल आते हैं, जो फफोले बन सकते हैं; ये आमतौर पर हल्के होते हैं और 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाते हैं, बताता है NHS [3][1]।

अभी के लिए: ठंडे तरल पदार्थ पिलाएँ (खट्टे जूस से बचें), दही जैसा मुलायम खाना दें, और गर्म, नमकीन व मसालेदार चीज़ें न दें [1]। मुँह के दर्द के लिए पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है — खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे से पूछें [1]।

डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ अगर:
- मुँह या होंठ के आसपास सूजन हो [6]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [6]
- गर्दन या सिर पर दाने निकलें और पूरे शरीर पर फैलें, जो खसरे जैसे लगें [1]
- दाने रेत जैसे खुरदुरे लगें, जो स्कार्लेट फीवर जैसे हों [1]

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [1] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "How to treat hand, foot and mou
[3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout
[6] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
दस्त या उल्टी के दौरान बच्चे को भूखा नहीं रखना चाहिए — वह सामान्य आहार ले सकता है, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करते हुए। दूध (स्तनपान) सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, और अगर बच्चा मांगे तो उससे भी अधिक बार दें [1]। डेयरी उत्पादों को रोकने की ज़रूरत नहीं है; तली-भुनी चीज़ें, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें क्योंकि उनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]।

पेशाब कम आना इस बात का संकेत हो सकता है कि बच्चा पर्याप्त तरल नहीं ले रहा — पेशाब का गाढ़ा या तेज़ महक वाला होना भी इसी वजह से हो सकता है [3]। ओआरएस (मौखिक रीहाइड्रेशन घोल) तैयार करके थोड़ा-थोड़ा, बार-बार देना इस स्थिति में मदद करता है [1]।

इन पर ध्यान दें और तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें:
- बहुत उल्टी होना, या तरल भी न पच पाना [1]
- उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो [1]
- पेशाब में जलन या दर्द, बुखार, कमर या पेट के निचले हिस्से में दर्द [3]
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE
[3] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "Urinary tract infections (UTI

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से जाँच ज़रूरी है, और SEUP के मुताबिक़ डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करके बताएँगे कि आगे कोई टेस्ट चाहिए या नहीं — ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

जब तक आप डॉक्टर के पास पहुँचें, बच्ची को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उस पर नज़र रखें। अगर वह उल्टी करे तो उसे करवट पर लिटाएँ ताकि उल्टी से दम न घुटे, और मुँह में कुछ न डालें। होश-हवास और व्यवहार पर ध्यान दें।

डॉक्टर को तुरंत दिखाएँ अगर:
- उम्र तीन महीने से कम हो [1]
- गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई हो [1]
- व्यवहार या हालत में कोई चिंता की बात दिखे [1]
- बार-बार उल्टी हो और तरल पदार्थ पेट में न रुके [3]
- बहुत तेज़ सिरदर्द, गर्दन में अकड़न, या रोशनी में देखने पर दर्द हो [3]

बच्ची को भूख-प्यास के हिसाब से थोड़ा-थोड़ा पानी या दूध दें, और उसे स्कूल या भीड़-भाड़ वाली जगह पर न भेजें जब तक उल्टी बंद न हो जाए [3]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS
[3] NHS — "Norovirus (vomiting bug)" (2024), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/co

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज के कारण बच्चा पॉटी करते समय रो सकता है — रोने के कई कारणों में से एक कब्ज भी है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें — कभी-कभी इसके अलावा ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं किया जा सकता, ऐसा NHS बताता है [1]। अगर समझ न आए कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

मदद कब लें — इन संकेतों पर तुरंत:
- रोने के बीच बच्चा सामान्य न हो, चिड़चिड़ा या सुस्त रहे [6]
- पीलापन, पसीना, सुस्ती या दूध/खाना न लेना [6]
- बुखार, उल्टी या मल में खून [6]
- रोना लगातार हो और शांत ही न हो, या आवाज़ सामान्य न लगे [4]
- बहुत तेज़ बुखार या दूध में रुचि न होना [4]
sources: [1] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby
[2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार में हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है और खासकर हाथ-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग दिखता है; जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना, लाल और गर्म हो जाता है [2]। बुखार शरीर का बचाव है, अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं [4]।

अभी: बच्चे को हल्के कपड़े पहनाएँ और ठंड न लगने दें; बुखार से परेशानी हो तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है, और खूब तरल देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है [5]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [7]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [7]
- त्वचा पर दाग़ हों जो दबाने पर न मिटें [7]
- मुँह से कुछ भी, ठोस या तरल, न ले पाए [7]
- बच्चा 2 महीने से छोटा हो या रोग-प्रतिरोधक क्षमता कम हो [7]
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",

[5] PUC Chile — "Manual de Pediatría", section "Fiebre", p. 314, 315
[7] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त हो जाना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना निमोनिया की गंभीरता के संकेतों में गिना जाता है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को खाने-पीने के लिए देते रहें और स्तनपान चालू रखें [2]। बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

खतरे के लक्षण:
- बुखार से दौरे पड़ना [2]
- खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना करना [2]
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना [2]
- सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आना [2]
- त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक [2]
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बहुत कम पेशाब आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में बच्चे को तुरंत डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [1]।

तब तक, बच्चे को थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार तरल दें, और खाना बंद न करें — सामान्य आहार जारी रखें, बस मात्रा कम और बार-बार दें [1]। अगर बच्चा स्तनपान करता है, तो दूध पिलाते रहें, और मांगे तो और भी बार [1]। चिकित्सकीय सलाह के बिना उपवास न कराएं [1]।

इन लक्षणों पर ध्यान दें और तुरंत मदद लें:
- बहुत उल्टी होना, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी न पचना, या बिना कुछ खाए भी उल्टी [1]
- उल्टी हरी हो, उसमें खून हो, या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो [1]

ये जानकारी SEUP के अनुसार है [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बुखार शरीर का संक्रमण से लड़ने का स्वाभाविक तरीका है, और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में अपने आप उतर जाता है [3]। तेज़ बुखार के साथ त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, गंभीर संक्रमण का संकेत हो सकते हैं [1]।

अभी यह करें:
- बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [2]।
- ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें और न ही स्पंज करें — बुखार संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]।
- 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।
- 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल न दें; 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वजन वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या डिहाइड्रेशन वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]।
- दवा की मात्रा उम्र और वजन पर निर्भर है — अपने डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार दें।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रियाशील या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [1]
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो [1]
- मुँह से कुछ भी न ले पाए [1]
- गर्दन अकड़ जाए, रोशनी से परेशानी हो, या दौरा पड़े [2]
- होंठ या त्वचा नीली, स्लेटी या सामान्य से पीली दिखे [2]

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar hai — paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein madad karta hai [1]. Dawa ki sahi matra bachche ke vazan par nirbhar karti hai, isliye vazan jaan kar hi dawa dein [2]. Aap PediBot ke dose calculator se paracetamol ki matra nikaal sakte hain.

Paracetamol har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Ibuprofen har 6 se 8 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, lekin 6 mahine se chhote bachchon ko na dein [2]. AEPap ke mutabik shuruaat paracetamol se karein [3]. Do alag antitérmicos ko baari-baari na dein — isse dose mein galti ho sakti hai [3].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Aapne packet ya leaflet se zyada paracetamol de diya ho [7]
- Bukhar 3-4 ghante baad bhi tez ho aur bechaini kam na ho [3]
- Vazan 3 kg se kam ho (paracetamol na dein) [3]
- 3 mahine se chhota ya 5 kg se kam vazan ho (ibuprofen na dein) [3]

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi aksar asthma ka lakshan ho sakti hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabiq bachon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. Bronchiolitis mein bhi raat ki khansi ho sakti hai [3].

Ghar par: kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer rakhein, bachche ko khoob paani pilayein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray istemal karein [6]. Khansi ke syrup, mucolytics, cortisone ya antibiotics se parhez karein — ye bronchiolitis mein faydemand nahi hain [2]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor se poochein [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans tez ya mushkil ho rahi ho [7]
- Honton ka rang neela-purple ho jaye [7]
- Doodh/khana lene mein dushwari, inkaar ya ulti [7]
- Paani kam ho, diaper sookha, munh sookha [7]
- Bachcha bahut sust ya rone wala ho [7]

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli ke liye, yeh heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakta hai — NHS ke mutabiq heat rash chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli aur halki sujan ke saath hota hai, aur yeh aam taur par kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Abhi kya karein: skin ko thanda rakhein taaki pasina na aaye — dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki rajai use karein, thande paani se nahayein, aur paani zyada pilayein [6]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur dane ko kuraidne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream na lagayein [6].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Munh ke aas-paas sujan ho ya saans lene mein dikkat ho [5]
- Dane bade, ubhre hue aur khujli wale ho jayein [5]
- Kuch dinon mein sudhar na ho [6]

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
text:
Bachche ka bed se girna aur ek baar ulti karna — giri ke baad ulti ho sakti hai, lekin is sthiti ke baare mein NHS ke paas koi khaas jaankari nahi hai. Agar ulti baar-baar ho, ya bachcha sust lage, to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai.

NHS ke mutabik, ulti aam taur par 1-2 din mein band ho jaati hai [1]. Tab tak:

- Chhote-chhote ghoont paani ya ORS ghol ke, thode-thode antar par do.
- Fruit juice ya fizzy drinks mat do — ye diarrhoea badha sakte hain [1].
- Formula ko patla mat karo, usual strength par hi banao [1].
- 12 saal se chhote bachche ko diarrhoea rokne ki dawa mat do [1].

Turant madad lein agar:
- 12 mahine se chhota bachcha ho aur aap chintit hain [5]
- Bachcha doodh/feed lena band kar de [5]
- Peshaab kam aaye, nappies sookhe rahein [5]
- Baar-baar ulti ho aur kuch bhi andar na ruke [5]
- Ulti mein khoon ho ya green/yellow-green ho [5]

Giri ke baad agar bachcha behosh, sust, ya aspasthai lage, to turant emergency department le jaayein.

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kabz mein potty karte waqt takleef aur rona aam baat hai, lekin iske baare mein in sources mein khaas tafseel nahi hai. NHS ke mutabiq, bacche ke rone ki ek wajah kabz bhi ho sakti hai [3]. Agar aapko samajh nahi aa raha ki kya galat hai, to apne doctor se baat karein [3].

Rone ki doosri aam wajuhaat: bhookh, gandha nappy, gas, thakan, ya god mein aana [4]. Kuch bacche feed ke waqt bhi rote hain; breastfeeding mein positioning theek karne se madad mil sakti hai [5].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Lagatar rona jo shaant na ho, ya rona normal na lage [7]
- Tez bukhaar ya doodh peene mein dilchaspi na ho [7]
- 8 ghante se peshaab geeLa nappy na ho [7]
- Skin, hoth ya jeebh neeli, grey ya pale ho [7]
- Saans lene mein dikkat [7]

text:
Bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai to yeh zaroori hai ki turant madad li jaye. SEUP ke mutabik, saans lene mein dikkat (pasliyan dikhna ya seene ka dhasna, tez saans, chalne ya daudne mein thakan) ek aisi cheez hai jise ghar par nazar rakhna chahiye aur iske hone par turant madad leni chahiye [7].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai, bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, aur unhe kuch bhi khilane-pilane ki koshish na karein. Agar bachche ko bukhar bhi hai, to unhe halke kapde pehnaayein aur thanda rakhein.

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat ho, pasliyan dikhein ya seene ka hissa andar ki taraf dhase [5]
- Saans lene mein rukawat ho ya saans ruk jaaye [5]
- Honth, jeebh ya chehra neela ya grey ho jaye [5]
- Bachcha bahut sust ho jaye ya jagane par bhi na jage [5]
- Bachcha doodh ya khana peena band kar de [5]

Yeh sab signs gambhir hain aur inhe ignore nahi karna chahiye.

banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी साँस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा ज़्यादा तेज़ी से साँस लेता है और साँस में घरघराहट होती है [3]। CDC कहता है कि RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है [2]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को थोड़ा-थोड़ा और बार-बार दूध या तरल दें, क्योंकि बीमारी में खाना-पीना कम हो जाता है [2][3]। बच्चे को सीधा और आराम से रखें, और उसकी साँस पर नज़र रखें [3]।

मदद कब लें — इनमें से कोई भी दिखे तो तुरंत:
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ़, पसलियाँ अंदर धँसना या घरघराहट [3]
- साँस लेते समय रुकावट या ठहराव [3]
- होंठ, जीभ या त्वचा नीली या स्लेटी पड़ना [3]
- बच्चा बहुत सुस्त हो और जागे नहीं [3]
- 12 घंटे से ज़्यादा सूखा नैपी या पानी की कमी के लक्षण [3]

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in whooping cough and croup, and both are usually worse at night [2][5]. For a 2 year old, keep the room cool and give small sips of fluid often to keep them comfortable [2].

Warning signs — get help if your child:
- has a very bad cough that is getting worse [4]
- is finding it hard to breathe properly (shallow breathing) [4]
- has lips, tongue, face or skin suddenly turn blue or grey [4]
- has chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- has seizures (fits) [4]

If your child has a barking cough like a seal, or a whoop sound between coughs, see your doctor — they may give medicine to shorten the illness [5][2].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by several different viral illnesses, and the pattern of the rash helps tell them apart. In measles, the rash usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days to the chest, arms, legs and feet, and it usually lasts four to eight days before fading on its own [4]. Chickenpox causes an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back before spreading, and it usually lasts five to ten days [5].

For the itching of chickenpox, calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help, and acetaminophen can help with fever — do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [5].

See a doctor if your child has:
- Fever with the rash [4]
- Trouble breathing or severe respiratory problems [4]
- Signs of dehydration from severe diarrhoea [4]
- Ear infection symptoms [4]
- Confusion, seizures or unusual sleepiness [4]

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
A child who eats very little for a while is a common reason to see the doctor, and in most cases no serious physical cause is found [4]. Loss of appetite can also come with infections such as hepatitis A, along with fever, tiredness, diarrhoea, nausea or tummy discomfort [5].

What to do now: keep offering food and fluids as usual, without forcing. If your child is not gaining weight, the doctor will look at what is behind it — sometimes a physical cause, often family, social or psychological difficulties, and many cases improve on their own after some time [6].

See your doctor if:
- Your child is not gaining weight or is losing weight [4][6]
- The poor eating has gone on every day for at least a month [6]
- Fever, diarrhoea, nausea, tummy pain, dark urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes [5]
- Your child seems very tired, weak or unwell [5]

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling sound when breathing is called wheezing, and in a 6-month-old it is most often caused by a viral respiratory infection, according to the SEUP [2][7]. Bronchiolitis, which affects babies under 2, usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and breathing difficulty can appear 2 to 4 days later [4].

What to do now: keep feeding your baby and offer fluids often, since babies with breathing trouble find it harder to feed [4]. Keep the nose clear of mucus so feeding is easier [4]. Do not give any cough or cold medicine — the dose of any medicine depends on your child's weight and must come from your doctor [4].

Get help if:
- Breathing gets faster or harder [4]
- The ribs pull in or the chest sinks with each breath [4][5]
- Your baby is too tired or irritable to feed [4][5]
- Lips, face or nails turn pale or bluish [6]
- Your baby becomes drowsy or hard to wake [5]

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप उतर जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें [3]। निर्जलीकरण के संकेत देखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, और रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखती रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर ही रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए सही है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें अगर वज़न 5 किलो से कम हो, चिकनपॉक्स हो या निर्जलीकरण हो [2]। बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

डॉक्टर से मदद लें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [2]
- बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के और संकेत [2]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]
- खाना न चाहे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [2]
- निर्जलीकरण — कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [2]

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या उसके शरीर को स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य कहता है [3]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा है [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने दिखें [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- बच्चा खाने को राज़ी न हो या स्तनपान न करे [3]
- बच्चा सुस्त हो जाए या ज़्यादा देर जागे नहीं [3]

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ("सिबिलेंस") श्वसन-मार्ग में रुकावट के कारण हो सकती है, जिसे ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से सुधार होता है, और प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में इसका मुख्य कारण श्वसन-संक्रमण होता है [2]। ऐसे लक्षणों वाले बच्चे को स्वास्थ्य-कर्मी से मिलना चाहिए [5]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को सीधा बैठाएँ और शांत रखें, और उसे कुछ भी खाने-पीने के लिए मजबूर न करें। सांस लेने में तकलीफ़, तेज़ सांस, पसली चलना या सीटी की आवाज़ बढ़ने पर तुरंत मदद लें [2][7]।

चेतावनी के संकेत — इनमें तुरंत मदद लें:
- तेज़ सांस या सांस लेने में गंभीर तकलीफ़ [7]
- पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना [2]
- चेहरे, होंठ या नाखूनों का पीला या नीला पड़ना [7]
- दूध या खाना न लेना [7]
- बेचैनी या चिड़चिड़ापन [7]

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं, और इनमें से कुछ घर पर ही ठीक हो जाती हैं। छोटे-छोटे बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने उन नन्हीं माइट्स से हो सकते हैं जो त्वचा में घुस जाती हैं (स्केबीज़), और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो सकता है [4]।

अभी यह करें: त्वचा को ठंडा रखें ताकि पसीना न आए और दाने में जलन न हो — ढीले सूती कपड़े पहनाएँ, हल्का बिस्तर लगाएँ, ठंडे पानी से नहलाएँ, और पानी खूब पिलाएँ [6]। खुजली या चुभन शांत करने के लिए ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, और खुजाने की जगह दानों को थपथपाएँ [6]। सुगंधित शावर जेल या क्रीम इस्तेमाल न करें [6]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों [1]
- घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का शक हो [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार, परतदार दाने हों [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, पर ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और मामूली उपचार से ठीक हो जाते हैं [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

टीके समय पर लगवाना ज़रूरी है, ताकि बच्चा गंभीर बीमारियों से बचा रहे [3]। अगर कोई टीका छूट जाए, तो अपने डॉक्टर से मिलें — वे बताएँगे कि कौन-सा टीका और कब लगवाना है [3]। भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर से पूछ लें कि आपके बच्चे की बारी कब है [4]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- टीके के बाद कोई गंभीर दुष्प्रभाव दिखे [6]
- बच्चा बहुत सुस्त या बेचैन लगे [6]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [6]

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi aksar asthma ka lakshan ho sakti hai: bachchon mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabiq asthma mein khansi ke saath saans phoolna, tez saans chalna aur seeti jaisi aawaz bhi ho sakti hai [1].

Ghar par: kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer lagaayein, aur bachche ko kaafi taral (paani, doodh) pilayein [4]. Khaansi ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein, kyunki kuch cough-cold dawaiyon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye theek nahi [4]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Tez ya mushkil saans, seene ka dhasna, pasliyan dikhna [7]
- Hothon ya chehre par neela rang, ya bachcha bahut sust/neend mein [7]
- Har 2 ghante ya usse zyada baar inhaler ki zaroorat [7]
- Khansee ke saath saans lene mein badi dikkat [5]

Agar khansi 10 din se zyada rahe ya behtar hone ke baad phir bigad jaaye, to doctor se milein [4].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Girne ke baad sar par chot lagne ke sabse aam lakshan sir dard, chakkar aana, ulti aur neend aana hain, SEUP ke mutabiq [1]. Ghar par 24 se 48 ghante aaram karayein, koi jismani khel ya mobile, tablet, video game bilkul nahi [2]. Doodh ya khana unki bhookh ke hisaab se jaari rakhein, koi khaas diet ki zaroorat nahi [6]. Agar sir dard ho to paracetamol ya ibuprofen unki doctor ki batayi hui khurak mein de sakte hain [6]. Zyada zaroori chot mein har 4 ghante mein jagakar dekhein [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Tez ya badhta sir dard, dawa se bhi na kam ho [2]
- Baar baar ulti [2]
- Bechaini ya jagane par na uthna [2]
- Baat ya chalne mein dikkat, vyavhaar mein badlav [2]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [2]

Zyadatar bachche jaldi theek ho jate hain [6].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche par red rashes ke liye, WHO ke mutabik khaas taur par chhote bachchon mein sarna (scabies) se hone wali eruption palms, soles aur scalp par zyada gambhir hoti hai [2]. Agar yeh rashes sarna hain, to iska ilaaj creams ya dawaiyon se hota hai [5].

Abhi ke liye: bachche ke nakhun chhote rakhein taaki khujli se skin na phate, aur unhe aaram se rakhein. Sarna ho to poore ghar ke logon ka ek saath ilaaj zaroori hota hai, kyunki yeh direct skin contact se phailta hai [5].

Doctor se milne ke signs:
- Raat mein tez khujli [2]
- Ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas line jaisi sujan [2]
- Skin par infection ya pus [2]
- Peshab mein kami ya sujan (kidney par asar) [2]

Yeh rashes measles bhi ho sakte hain, jismein bukhar, khansi aur aankhon se paani aana bhi hota hai [3].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai — bachchon ko polio se bachane ke liye polio vaccine (VPI) di jaati hai, aur ise samay par dena chahiye [3]. Spain ke national schedule ke mutabik polio vaccine 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein di jaati hai, aur 6 saal ki umar par ek booster bhi diya jaata hai [3]. Agar bachcha 2, 4, 6 aur 18 mahine par 4 doses le chuka hai, to 6 saal par polio ke bina dTpa diya jaata hai [3].

Kuch bachchon ko khaas dhyan ki zaroorat hoti hai — jaise bahut kam umar ke ya risk wale newborns — unme bhi inactivated vaccines bina der ke di jaani chahiye [2]. Agar aapke bachche ki vaccination adhoori reh gayi hai, to apne doctor se mil kar pending doses poore karwaayein [1].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- Bachche ko bukhar ya kamzori ho [7]
- Saans lene mein dikkat ho [7]
- Koi bhi vaccine reaction ke baad serious lakshan dikhein [7]

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection of the gut, and the main risk is dehydration — the younger the child, the greater that risk [1]. The World Health Organization says the key treatment is rehydration with oral rehydration salts (ORS), a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar, plus zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [2]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace losses, and do not give anti-diarrhoeal or anti-vomiting medicines without asking your paediatrician [1]. Offer food in smaller amounts more often, avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices, and keep breastfeeding normally or more often if your baby wants it [7].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Very watery, frequent stools and unable to drink fast enough [1]
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or lots of blood in the stool [1]

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार, डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का इंजेक्शन लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव आम हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं, जो अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

इंजेक्शन के एक-दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है; खुराक के बारे में इंजेक्शन देने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के हिसाब से खुराक तय होती है।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

टीकाकरण की उम्र भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body can't cool itself, usually after too long in the sun or heat, according to the SEUP [1]. Dizziness is one of the symptoms it lists [1].

What to do now: move your child to a cool, shaded place and take off extra clothing. Put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to help bring the temperature down [6]. Do not give fever medicines for heat illness — physical cooling measures are used instead, according to the AEPap [5].

Get help if:
- Fever above 39°C that doesn't come down with home measures [7]

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text:
Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are introduced alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts and increase gradually as your baby grows [3].

Offer just a few pieces or teaspoons of food at first — babies have tiny tummies and do not need 3 meals a day yet [2]. Pick a relaxed time when your baby is not too tired, and offer food before their usual milk feed, but not when they are too hungry [2]. Let them set the pace, and keep offering new foods even if rejected — it can take 10 tries or more [2]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays their main drink and main source of energy in the first year [2]. From around 6 months, offer sips of water with meals from an open or free-flow cup [2].

Aim for 2–3 meals a day at 6–8 months [3].

See your doctor if your baby is not growing well or you are worried about feeding [3].

q: my 6 month old has started eating food, what should I give first

Around 6 months is the right time to start solid foods, and how much your baby eats at first matters less than getting them used to eating [2]. They will still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

q: my 4 year old child has small red bumps on face and neck
text:
Small red bumps starting on the face and spreading down to the neck can be the rash of measles, which usually begins on the face at the hairline and moves downward, according to the CDC [3]. The WHO says this rash appears 3 to 5 days after the first symptoms and lasts 4 to 8 days before fading on its own [6].

Watch for the earlier signs in the days before the rash: fever, runny nose, cough, red watery eyes, and tiny white spots inside the cheeks [6].

Get medical help if you see:
- Fever spiking above 104°F when the rash appears [3]
- Trouble breathing, or a severe ear infection [6]
- Diarrhea with signs of dehydration [6]
- Confusion, drowsiness, or a rash that worries you [6]

Most children recover, but measles can cause complications, especially in children under five [6].

q: my 1 year old baby body is very hot since morning
text:
A fever is a body temperature above normal, usually around 37 °C, and it is not an illness in itself — it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers last 2 to 4 days, and it is normal for the temperature not to come all the way down after a fever medicine [2].

Give plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [1]. If the fever is high, your doctor may recommend an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen; never give aspirin to a child with fever [1]. The dose depends on your child's weight — for paracetamol and ibuprofen you can use PediBot's dose calculator.

See a doctor if your child:
- is listless, barely responsive or very irritable [7]
- has trouble breathing [7]
- has skin spots that do not fade when pressed [7]
- will not take solids or liquids by mouth [7]

q: my baby has vomiting and loose motion since morning
text:
Vomiting and loose stools together are usually caused by a stomach bug or food poisoning, according to the NHS [1]. It is usually not serious, but babies can get dehydrated, so the main job today is fluids [3][4].

Keep breastfeeding or formula feeding as normal, and offer it more often if your baby wants it — do not water down formula [5][6]. Give oral rehydration solution in small, frequent sips; the amount depends on your baby's weight, so follow the dose your doctor or pharmacist gives you [4]. Do not give fruit juice, fizzy drinks or sports drinks, and no medicine to stop the diarrhoea [5][6].

Get help now if:
- Your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [2]
- Vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [2][5]
- Sleepy, floppy, very thirsty, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or fewer wet nappies [2][3]
- Vomiting a lot, or unable to keep any fluids down [2][5]
- Diarrhoea lasting more than a day, or any fever in an infant [3]

q: my son has fast breathing with cough
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Fast breathing with a cough can be a sign of a respiratory infection, and the SEUP notes that in bronchiolitis, breathing difficulty can appear 2 to 4 days after a cold starts, with faster breathing and trouble feeding [3]. Keep your child resting semi-upright and offer fluids often in small amounts, since feeding difficulty is one of the things to watch [7].

Watch for these signs, which mean your child needs to be seen:
- Breathing getting harder: ribs pulling in, chest sinking, belly moving with each breath [3][6]
- Very drowsy, floppy or very irritable [2][6]
- Chest or side pain when breathing [2][6]
- Poor colour [6]
- Refusing food and fluids repeatedly [6]

The CDC also advises seeking care for fast or troubled breathing, dehydration, or a fever lasting more than 4 days [4].

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes, paracetamol (Calpol) can help if your child is distressed or uncomfortable because of a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It also relieves pain from teething, earache, sore throat and colds [3].

Give it at the dose recommended by your paediatrician, every 6 to 8 hours; ibuprofen works similarly and can be used instead [1]. Treat your child's discomfort, not the fever number itself [1]. Keep them well hydrated with plenty of fluids, in a neutral, ventilated room, and don't over-wrap them [1]. Don't force food if they don't want it [1]. Don't use cold water baths or wet cloths — they're unpleasant and don't work [1]. Never give aspirin to a child with fever [2].

See a doctor if your child:
- is floppy, barely responsive or very irritable [7]
- has trouble breathing [7]
- has spots that don't fade when pressed [7]
- won't take solids or fluids by mouth [7]

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text:
Yes — oral rehydration salts (ORS) are one of the key treatments for diarrhoea, according to the WHO [1]. Give ORS as a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar; it is absorbed in the small intestine and replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, or sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness, or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Very watery, heavy, frequent stools and the child cannot drink fast enough to keep up [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: son placas rojas y elevadas que pican mucho, y en la infancia la mayoría están causadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. También puede tratarse de una reacción a picaduras de insectos, que da lesiones que pican intensamente y aparecen sobre todo en brazos y piernas, según Ecimed [6].

Mientras tanto: evita que se rasque, porque el rascado frecuente puede infectar las lesiones [6]. No pongas cremas ni medicamentos por tu cuenta; el tratamiento lo indica el médico [3].

Consulta a tu doctor si:
- La piel se infecta (supura, se pone muy roja o caliente) [6]
- Aparece hinchazón de manos, pies, codos o cara [3]
- Le cuesta respirar o tragar [3]
- Tiene fiebre o se ve decaído [6]

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis con los ojos pegados al despertar es muy frecuente en niños, según la SEUP [3]. Para las legañas, limpia los párpados con agua tibia y una gasa limpia, de dentro hacia fuera, usando una gasa distinta para cada ojo.

Consulta a tu pediatra si:
- El ojo está muy rojo, duele o hay inflamación [3].
- Aparece enrojecimiento, dolor o inflamación detrás de la oreja [3].
- El niño está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable [3].
- Tiene mal estado general o fiebre alta [3].
- No mejora en 48-72 horas [3].

q: se le marcan las costillas al respirar pero luego se pone a jugar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado); Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
Que se le marquen las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria, según la SEUP [3][4]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño incorporado y tranquilo, y no le des jarabes ni supositorios para la tos sin consultar [7].

Señales que indican que está peor:
- Respira cada vez más deprisa o se le hunde el pecho [5][7].
- Está muy agitado, decaído o somnoliento [4][5].
- Se pone morado o pálido, o tiene mal color [4][5].
- Le cuesta tragar o babea mucho [7].
- Rechaza la alimentación y los líquidos [4].

Aunque luego se ponga a jugar, la dificultad para respirar es motivo de consulta urgente [2][4].

q: no hay quien despierte a mi hijo y respira muy raro
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: No responde a estímulos
text:
Si no responde y respira de forma anormal, hay que actuar ya: ponlo de lado y no le pongas nada en la boca, según la SEUP [3]. Mientras llega la ayuda, vigila que siga respirando y no lo dejes solo [3].

Señales de alarma que confirman la gravedad:
- Coloración azul de cara o labios [3].
- Dificultad respiratoria o cambios en la forma de respirar [3].
- Somnolencia excesiva o problemas para despertarlo [3].
- Alteraciones del comportamiento, muy irritable o no puede parar de llorar [3].
- Vómitos muy repetidos [3].

Si está muy agitado o somnoliento, o se pone morado o pálido, es una urgencia [2].
